Executive Summary

What the business is

NVIDIA sells connected computing platforms—GPUs, networking, systems and software—to cloud providers, server makers and businesses. A GPU is a processor that handles many tasks at once; a cloud provider rents computing power and storage over the internet. Fiscal 2026 revenue was $215,938 million, led by Data Center.

What is the Bloomberg Terminal price per year?

Vendr, a software-buying marketplace, puts it at $24,000 to $27,000 per terminal a year for one to five terminals, about $2,000 a month. Godel Discount, a buying guide, puts one seat at $31,980 a year, $2,665 a month. Both read on November 4, 2026; Bloomberg publishes neither.

Is a Bloomberg Terminal worth it for stock research?

For most individual investors, no: you can research a company without one. A Terminal is for prices that update by the second and a chat with other traders; a report is a snapshot of one company.

Pay for a Terminal if…

  • you trade or manage money all day;
  • you need prices that update by the second;
  • you deal through its chat with other traders.

A full report fits if…

  • you are researching one company before you buy;
  • you want its numbers, risks and price cases, each with its source;
  • you want to start without a subscription.

Why is a Bloomberg Terminal so expensive?

A Terminal is a whole trading workplace, and you pay for all of it. Godel Discount lists what the money buys:

  • PricesReal-time data from 350+ exchanges, across stocks, bonds, currencies, commodities and derivatives.
  • NewsBloomberg News.
  • ResearchBloomberg Intelligence, research on 2,000+ companies.
  • ChatInstant Bloomberg, the network where bond trades are negotiated. Godel Discount argues the chat network is the core product.

A trader uses all of it every day. A long-term investor uses a small slice and still pays for the whole.

Not for one person: Godel Discount says Bloomberg has “no discounted individual or retail tier”, and a Terminal is a live market screen for professionals.

Executive Summary

What the business is

NVIDIA sells connected computing platforms—GPUs, networking, systems and software—to cloud providers, server makers and businesses. A GPU is a processor that handles many tasks at once; a cloud provider rents computing power and storage over the internet. Fiscal 2026 revenue was $215,938 million, led by Data Center. A dollar comes in when a direct customer buys a platform or software, while a cloud provider may rent its resulting capacity to an AI company or business. Software may be licensed, subscribed to or included with hardware.

  • Concentration: Data Center produced $193,737 million in fiscal 2026, versus $16,042 million from Gaming and $2,349 million from Automotive.
  • Platform economics: A sale can bundle GPUs, networking and CUDA, NVIDIA’s software tools for programming GPUs. NVIDIA does not disclose separate software revenue or renewal rates.
  • Outsourced production: NVIDIA designs products but relies on specialists for fabrication, packaging, memory, testing and assembly. Supply and capacity commitments reached $279 billion at July 2026.
  • Cash timing: Sales can precede cash. Days sales outstanding reached 60 days, and five direct customers represented 70% of accounts receivable at July 2026.

The challenges

  • Customer payback: Cloud providers must recover equipment, networking, power, cooling, staff and financing costs through paid workloads or savings. Low utilization or weak returns could pause the next spending cycle.
  • Platform substitution: CUDA familiarity can make switching costly, but customers may port workloads to AMD ROCm or custom chips. The risk is greatest if alternatives deliver better economics on real workloads.
  • System delivery and supply: A platform needs processors, memory, networking, assembly, power and cooling to arrive together. NVIDIA’s $279 billion of commitments increases the cost of a demand or product mismatch.
  • Export restrictions: Policy can block sales after inventory and supplier commitments are in place. NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion H20 charge after U.S. export restrictions.
